Reran run_momentum_backtest.py's exact logic sweeping low_liq round-trip cost 118/90/60/40/25bps, high_liq (23bps) and mid_liq (32.5bps) held fixed. Momentum net CAGR: 30.43% (118bps) -> 30.68% (40bps) -> 30.73% (25bps, full ~21x calibration). Margin over benchmark: 12.32 -> 12.57 -> 12.62 pts. Effect is small (+0.25 to +0.30 pts of CAGR across the full plausible range) because low_liq names are only ~10.5% of top-decile momentum's mean composition (58.3% high_liq, 31.2% mid_liq, 10.5% low_liq, measured directly across all 31 rebalances) -- the tercile FINDINGS.md flagged as the dataset's most uncertain cost input turns out to have limited leverage on the headline result specifically because momentum's own top decile is liquidity-tilted toward larger names already. Consequence: even if 118bps is wrong by ~4-5x, it does not change Study 1's holdout pass/fail conclusion or materially revise the headline CAGR. Does not resolve whether low-liq names are individually tradeable at realistic size -- that is a per-name execution question, not a portfolio-CAGR one. No study slot spent.

universe: pre-holdout backtest NAV series, 2017-2024, benchmark peak-to-trough threshold fixed before inspection
notes: Reframe of FINDINGS.md Section 4's ad hoc '2020 specifically' example into an exhaustive, criterion-first pass: benchmark drawdown episodes exceeding 15% peak-to-trough, defined mechanically off the benchmark NAV, not hand-picked. RESULT: exactly 1 episode in the whole series (peak 2017-11-15, trough 2020-03-05, recovery 2021-03-10, benchmark -49.82% peak-to-trough). Momentum finished the FULL episode net ahead: +42.23% vs bench +9.56% (+32.68pts). Split at the actual trough (not a calendar boundary): decline leg mom -35.95%/bench -49.82% (+13.87pts, consistent with Section 3's downside-protection mechanism); recovery leg (trough to recovery) mom +122.07%/bench +118.35% (+3.73pts) -- does NOT show Section 4's ~20pt underperformance. Reconciled directly: Section 4's -19.8pt figure is calendar-year-2020 (Jan-Dec), a DIFFERENT window that excludes the 2021Q1 rebalance the mechanical recovery leg includes and includes the 2020-03-05 rebalance the mechanical split assigns to the decline leg instead (that date is the series' actual trough). Calendar-year-2020 number reconfirmed unchanged and still correct under its own windowing (+45.9%/+65.7%/-19.8pts). Secondary 10% threshold finds one more episode (2021-09-15 peak/2022-03-17 trough, bench -14.71%), also net ahead for momentum (+6.38pts). CONSEQUENCE: FINDINGS.md Section 4 amended in place -- 'opportunity cost in a violent recovery' is more window-dependent than originally stated; neither mechanically-defined drawdown episode in this one pre-holdout series (n=2, descriptive only, no significance claim) shows momentum behind the benchmark once the window is drawn from the market's own peak/trough rather than a calendar boundary. Does not overturn the calendar-year number or resolve whether a recovery-leg cost survives a mechanical window -- one episode is not enough data to settle it either way, stated as a real limitation. No study slot spent.
